SI-4_title.answer: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS) for normative modelling of age-related cortical thickness effects. The local width or smoothing kernel of the regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization across 5-100% of the full age range using Brent's method.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS), where the local width or smoothing kernel of the regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization across 5-100% of the full age range using Brent's method as implemented in the R optim function from the stats package.

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT) was the primary response variable, extracted using FreeSurfer (v5.3.0) across 308 cortical regions. CT was defined as the shortest distance between vertices of the GM/WM boundary and the pial surface.
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: Here we focus specifically on a neural feature of cortical morphology known as CT. CT is a well-studied neuroanatomical feature thought to be differentially affected in autism and has received increasing attention in recent years. ... CT of each vertex was defined as the shortest distance between vertices of the GM/WM boundary and the pial surface. ... All analyses were done on CT averaged within 308 cortical regions.
NM2-2_response_variable.location: Bethlehem2020.pdf.md: Introduction and Methods / Imaging processing and quantification

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: In the normative LOESS model, age was the primary explanatory variable. The model estimated age-specific mean and standard deviation for cortical thickness to compute w-scores. Additional covariates (site as random effect, sex, age, in-scanner head motion, and Euler index) were included in the linear mixed effects case-control analysis but not directly in the LOESS normative model itself.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group (TD) ... For each age bin and every brain region we computed a normative mean and standard deviation from the TD group. This was done separately for each sex, given known sex differential developmental trajectories.
